title: LLM Voting: Human Choices and AI Collective Decision-Making

paper.authors: Joshua C. Yang, Damian Dailisan, Marcin Korecki, Carina I. Hausladen, Dirk Helbing
paper.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES) 7
paper.repo: https://github.com/ethz-coss/LLM_voting (code + all LLM votes/outcomes); human data: https://github.com/joshuay1/zurich-pb-voting
paper.repo_license: none (no LICENSE file in either repo)

dependence.note: 180 LLM agents stand in for the 180 human participants of a Zurich participatory-budgeting experiment (24 projects, CHF 60,000); every result compares LLM votes with the archived human votes. No new humans are needed.

claim.statement: GPT-4 Turbo agents voting on the 24 Zurich PB projects produce collective outcomes only moderately aligned with the human outcome - Kendall's tau = 0.39 at temperature 1.0 (0.37 at 1.5; Figure 7A) - and much less diverse than human voters (mean Jaccard dissimilarity between individual votes 0.44 at t = 1.0 vs 0.67 at t = 1.5, Figure 7B; approval counts concentrated around a median of 5 projects vs a 2-24 range for humans, Figure 3); no temperature preserves both diversity and human-likeness (Conclusion).
claim.metric: Kendall's tau between LLM and human aggregate project rankings (5-approval baseline; Borda for ranked votes); Jaccard dissimilarity between individual vote sets; distribution of the number of approved projects
claim.original_source: Results 'Diversity in Different Temperature Settings' and Figure 7 (AIES version, p. 1703); Figure 3; released outcome files outcome/gpt_temp/*/outcome.csv and votes.json

protocol.model_status: DEAD - shut down 2026-03-26 (target_models.json). The census hit 'gpt-4-turbo' is the product name only; gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 was not an arm.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (llm/api.py chat_request); LLaMA-2 70B Q8_0 via a local llama.cpp-style server
protocol.prompt_source: scripts/pb_voting_basic.py (project-list CSV block, voting instructions), agent/agent.py (initial context), data/lab_persona.csv (persona sentences); Figure 2 and Appendix C of the paper
protocol.messages: Initial Context (same instructions/background as the human experiment) [+ persona: 'You are a university student from Nord district in Zurich. In urban topics, you have a strong preference for transport. ...'] [+ CoT reflection turn before seeing the projects] -> Voting Prompt with the 24-project table and one instruction: 'Select any number of projects.' | 'Select exactly 5 projects.' | 'Distribute 10 points among the projects you like. List each of the project id you choose and the points you allocate together.' | 'Select 5 projects and rank them from the most preferred to the 5th most preferred.'; votes parsed by regex on '#<id>'
protocol.n_items: 180 agents per condition; conditions: 4 voting methods, reversed order / reversed IDs, 5 temperatures, persona, CoT
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: parse votes -> aggregate (Borda for ranks, normalised cumulative points) -> Kendall tau vs the human outcome (outcome/lab_vote/*.csv), Jaccard similarity/distance vs human individual votes (outcome/analyse_outcome.ipynb).
protocol.environment_check: Recompute tau = 0.39 / dissimilarity 0.44 from the released votes.json + human data before any call.

budget.assumptions: sibling arm, full design: 180 agents x ~14 conditions (4 methods + 2 order variants + 5 temperatures + persona + 2 CoT turns) = 2,520 calls per seed x 3 seeds; ~650 input tokens (context + 24-project table), ~120 output tokens. Core subset only (5-approval at t = 1.0 and 1.5): 360 calls per seed, ~$3 for 3 seeds.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (sibling arm only): survival if Kendall tau (GPT vs human, 5-approval, t = 1.0) stays 'moderate' (within +/- 0.15 of 0.39, bootstrap over agents) and the diversity ordering holds (dissimilarity at t = 1.5 > t = 1.0, both below the human level); partial if tau leaves the band but stays in (0.1, 0.8) with the diversity ordering intact; death if tau <= 0 or the LLM becomes as diverse as humans while matching them (tau >= 0.8).
judgment.notes: Kendall tau over 24 projects has a wide sampling distribution; report a CI from bootstrapping agents.

user_checks: Approve a sibling-snapshot arm (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) for the core subset (5-approval at t = 1.0/1.5, ~$3) or the full design (~$76)?
Confirm the core-claim choice (tau 0.39 / diversity trade-off) versus the ordering/labeling bias claims (reversed order and reversed IDs, Figure 4) or the persona-alignment claim (Figures 5-6).
Contact the authors about licensing the released votes for redistribution.
domain_notes: The human baseline is a lab experiment with 180 ETH/UZH students (payoff-linked PB vote, March 2023), so 'human' preferences are those of a specific student sample. Kendall tau is computed on aggregate rankings of 24 projects; Jaccard on individual vote sets. Temperature is the paper's lever for diversity, so successor endpoints that fix temperature (reasoning models) cannot reproduce the sweep.
